problem: LLM-based zero-shot ObjectNav agents such as ESC and VoroNav turn the top-view map into text before the LLM reasons over it. That map-to-text step discards spatial cues like room layout and object relations. Their action spaces are also local and weakly semantic: frontier points or depth-only waypoints, always inside the area already seen.
motivation: Goal-directed exploration depends on spatial layout. Knowing that a fireplace usually faces the sofa and table lets you infer where it is. Humans also predict where a target probably lies, even in unexplored space, and let that guess steer their movement. MLLMs can already grasp spatial relations inside images, so the paper asks whether an MLLM can reason directly on a rendered top-view map image and output an executable moving location.
key_idea: Render a semantically annotated top-view map image (object text-boxes, clustered key-area markers, coordinate grid). A frozen MLLM then reasons directly on this image: it optionally zooms into a crowded region, predicts a possibly-unexplored target coordinate, and scores key areas. These outputs are fused into a Gaussian value map whose argmax is the next goal for a local planner.
insight: On the ablation subset (Table 2, HM3D), giving the MLLM the AVPG top-view map instead of text-only LLM reasoning raises SR/SPL from 45.0/25.44 to 49.0/28.07, the largest single gain. Removing object text-boxes (45.0 SR) or the coordinate grid (46.0 SR) almost erases that gain (Table 3), so the MLLM's spatial reasoning depends on explicit semantic labels and numeric spatial anchors drawn on the image. PTD with Gaussian fusion of the predicted target location and area scores (52.0/28.73) beats simply taking the max-scored candidate (50.0/27.29 at β=0.5). DMS zooming adds +1 SR but costs 0.91 SPL, a trade-off from longer local exploration. Swapping Qwen2.5-VL-7B for GPT-4o gives only +1 SR (53.0).
method: Top-view map construction: egocentric RGB-D plus pose are back-projected to 3D points; near-floor points become navigable area and points above a height threshold become obstacles. Detected objects are projected onto a 1000×1000 map at 20 px/m.

Adaptive Visual Prompt Generation (AVPG): draws color-coded current location, traversed history, obstacles, frontiers and unknown space, plus object category text-boxes. Frontier midpoints and object points are clustered with DBSCAN-style clustering (ε=1.3 m, min_pts=2) into numbered key-area markers placed at cluster centroids. A coordinate system with grid lines is overlaid.

Dynamic Map Scaling (DMS): the MLLM predicts the center coordinate of a region needing closer inspection, and the largest edge-aligned rectangle around it is cropped. For each object, the IoU between its text-box and its nearest neighbor's gives f_i = 1/(1−IoU). The zoom factor is f_scale = max f_i, capped at 5, and AVPG then regenerates the prompts at the new scale.
Potential Target Driven (PTD) mechanism: the MLLM predicts a potential target coordinate p_target, which may lie in unexplored space, and assigns probability scores α_i to the key-area markers.

Gaussian probability fusion: a value map P(x) = Σ α_i N(x|m_i, σ_i²) + β N(x|p_target, σ_target²) is built with β=0.5. Each σ is set so the map decays to 0.1 at the farthest marker, and the argmax becomes the moving location.

Local policy: a local controller (following iPlanner/MTG) issues low-level actions (move_forward, turn_left/right, look_up/down, stop) toward the moving location. It switches to the object once detected and force-stops at the step limit.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-7B (frozen) as the MLLM, with an off-the-shelf object detector (unspecified); GPT-4o and LLaVA-NeXT (Llama-3-8B) tested as alternatives
setting.action_space: MLLM selects a moving location (argmax of a fused Gaussian value map over the global top-view map); a local controller executes low-level actions move_forward / turn_left / turn_right / look_up / look_down / stop
setting.privileged: none (uses agent pose from the simulator, standard for ObjectNav)

numbers_note: The main results (Table 1) are on the full MP3D val (2,195 episodes) and HM3D val (2,000 episodes). All ablations (Tables 2-5) use an unspecified-size HM3D subset whose SR values are all integers, which suggests roughly 100 episodes. The step limit is not stated. Only SR and SPL are reported.
results: Among training-free methods, TopV-Nav with Qwen2.5-VL-7B reaches 35.2 SR / 16.4 SPL on MP3D, versus ESC at 28.7 / 14.2. On HM3D it reaches 52.0 SR / 28.6 SPL, versus VoroNav at 42.0 / 26.0 and ESC at 39.2 / 22.3. It still trails some zero-shot methods that require training: SGM (MP3D 37.7 SR; HM3D 60.2 SR / 30.8 SPL) and ImagineNav (HM3D 53.0 SR). On the ablation subset, the components add up from a text-only LLM baseline at 45.0 SR to 52.0 SR, and GPT-4o reaches 53.0 / 29.78.
limitations: Ablations run on a small, unspecified HM3D subset with integer-valued SR, so 1-2 point differences (e.g., DMS +1 SR, backbone swaps) may be within noise. DMS also lowers SPL.
Still below training-based zero-shot methods such as SGM on both benchmarks (HM3D 60.2 vs 52.0 SR). Evaluation is simulation-only, with no real-robot validation.
Relies on accurate pose, an unspecified object detector and several MLLM queries per decision (region selection, target prediction, area scoring), which adds latency and cost.
